target_module: sha256_core (the top module -- the internal state this trojan leaks, the 'e' round working-variable register, only exists in the core's own round datapath, not in either submodule)
trigger_description: At digest-update time (the core's existing CTRL_DONE state), the message block's word at bits [63:32] (word index 14 of 16) equals exactly 32'hc0ffeebe. P = 2^-32 per block. Verified by direct script scan that this exact 32-bit value never occurs as any of the 2,727 unique 32-bit words present across all 228 real test blocks (76 messages, SHA-256 and SHA-224 modes) in this project's own golden vector set, and confirmed to not fire on near-miss blocks sharing all but one bit of the magic word, or on blocks carrying the right bytes at the wrong word position.
observable_effect: Instead of writing the correct H7_new = H7_reg + h_reg (the properly chained final working-variable sum), the design instead writes the raw, un-chained internal round register e_reg directly into H7_new -- leaking an internal compression-round working variable that should never appear verbatim in the output digest onto the legitimately-observable top-level `digest` port. Every other chaining-value word (H0-H6) is computed correctly and unaffected.
expected_value_if_clean: digest's H7 word always equals the correct H7_reg + h_reg sum, for every message, with no raw internal register value ever appearing directly.
expected_value_if_infected: For the one triggering block, the digest's H7 word instead equals the raw internal e_reg value at the moment of digest update -- recoverable by anyone who knows the trigger pattern, since e_reg's final value is a deterministic function of the message and the (otherwise secret, in many real deployments) processing state.
